title: SSO (OpenID Connect)
description: Checks an OpenID Connect identity provider and the app that signs in through it: the discovery document and JWKS are published and well-formed, the token endpoint issues client-credentials tokens and rejects a wrong secret, the sign-in page reaches the IdP, the session cookie carries Secure and HttpOnly, and the session is really dead after logout. The IdP form selectors default to Keycloak's; change them for Okta, Entra ID or Auth0.

variables.name: OIDC_ISSUER
variables.description: Issuer URL, without a trailing slash (e.g. https://idp.example.com/realms/acme).

variables.name: OIDC_TOKEN_ENDPOINT
variables.description: Token endpoint from the discovery document.

variables.name: OIDC_CLIENT_ID
variables.description: Client id of a confidential client allowed the client_credentials grant.

variables.name: OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET
variables.description: That client's secret. Stored as a project secret.

variables.name: OIDC_SCOPE
variables.description: Scope to request with client credentials.

variables.name: APP_LOGIN_URL
variables.description: Your app's sign-in URL; it should redirect to the IdP.

variables.name: IDP_USERNAME
variables.description: A test user that can sign in to the app.

variables.name: IDP_PASSWORD
variables.description: That test user's password. Stored as a project secret.

variables.name: IDP_USERNAME_SELECTOR
variables.description: Username field on the IdP sign-in form.

variables.name: IDP_PASSWORD_SELECTOR
variables.description: Password field on the IdP sign-in form.

variables.name: IDP_SUBMIT_SELECTOR
variables.description: Submit button on the IdP sign-in form.

variables.name: APP_SESSION_COOKIE
variables.description: Name of the app's session cookie after sign-in.

variables.name: APP_PROTECTED_URL
variables.description: A URL that needs a signed-in session (e.g. https://app.example.com/api/me).

variables.name: APP_LOGOUT_URL
variables.description: The app's logout endpoint (called with POST; edit the step if yours is GET).

suites.name: SSO (OpenID Connect)
suites.description: OIDC provider contract and the relying party's session handling.

cases.name: Discovery document and JWKS are published
cases.description: /.well-known/openid-configuration answers 200 with the fields every client needs, and its jwks_uri serves at least one key.

cases.name: Token endpoint issues client-credentials tokens
cases.description: A confidential client gets an access token; the token is kept in a runtime variable and never logged.

cases.name: Token endpoint rejects a wrong client secret
cases.description: RFC 6749 section 5.2: a bad client secret yields error=invalid_client.

cases.name: Sign-in page reaches the identity provider
cases.description: Opening the app's sign-in URL lands on the IdP form.

cases.name: Session cookie is Secure and HttpOnly
cases.description: After signing in through the IdP the app's session cookie carries Secure and HttpOnly. Add a sameSite expectation to the step if your app pins one.

cases.name: Session is dead after logout
cases.description: The pre-logout cookies are replayed against a protected URL after logging out; the server must refuse them (401/403/440 or a redirect to sign-in), not just clear the browser's cookie.
